_comment: THE most important alert in this project. Pod-health alerting cannot detect a pod that is Ready and returns 500 to every request. Requires Managed Prometheus, or a log-based metric (see below).

documentation.content:
MORE THAN 1% OF REQUESTS ARE FAILING.

What this means: users are getting errors RIGHT NOW. Kubernetes may show every pod as healthy - that is exactly the scenario this alert exists for.

First command:
  ./scripts/health-check.sh -n orders

Investigation path: docs/INCIDENT_HTTP_500.md
  1. Quantify - what %, since when, which endpoints?
  2. Correlate with deploys: helm history orders-api -n orders
  3. Is it ONE pod or ALL pods?
       kubectl logs -n orders -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=orders-api --tail=1000 \n         | jq -r 'select(.status>=500) | .pod' | sort | uniq -c
  4. Check for a mixed fleet: ./scripts/verify-version.sh -n orders -r orders-api -v VERSION

Resolution: if it correlates with a recent deploy, ROLL BACK FIRST.
  ./scripts/rollback.sh -n orders
Stopping user impact takes priority over root-causing.
